item.title: Sesshu Garden, Yamaguchi: A Zen Master's Design — Guide
item.description: The garden known as Sesshu Teien, in the grounds of Joei-ji temple in Yamaguchi city, is traditionally attributed to Sesshu Toyo, the fifteenth-century painter-monk regarded as one of the greatest masters of Japanese ink painting. Laid out as a strolling and viewing garden behind the temple, it composes moss, carefully placed stones, clipped shrubs and a quiet pond into a serene landscape meant to be contemplated much like one of Sesshu’s paintings.

item.title: Yamaguchi Chochin Lantern Festival — Guide
item.description: The Yamaguchi Gion Chochin Matsuri is the city’s great summer festival, a tradition some six hundred years old in which central Yamaguchi is lit by tens of thousands of glowing red paper lanterns. Strung in dense curtains along the main streets, over shrines and on lantern-decked poles and floats, their warm red light transforms the city into a magical scene after dark. The festivities include a lantern-lit dance in which performers move among the swaying lights, processions and shrine rites, all held over a couple of evenings in early August.

item.title: Yamaguchi City Culture and Arts Center — Guide
item.description: Yamaguchi city, the prefectural capital, has long prided itself on culture, once nicknamed the ‘Kyoto of the West’ for its refinement in the medieval era. Today that spirit continues in its modern cultural and arts facilities, which host changing exhibitions, concerts and performances, and programmes of international exchange, all in a contemporary setting in the heart of the city. For travellers, a stop here offers a glimpse of the region’s living cultural scene beyond its historic temples and gardens — a chance to catch an exhibition or event, learn about local arts, and see how a quiet provincial capital keeps its long cultural tradition alive in the present day.

item.title: Yuda Onsen: Yamaguchi City's White Fox Hot Spring — Guide
item.description: Yuda Onsen is a convenient and welcoming hot-spring resort right within Yamaguchi city, making it one of the easiest onsen stays in the region to reach. Legend says the springs were discovered when a white fox was seen healing an injury in the warm water, and the white fox has been the town’s mascot ever since, appearing on statues and footbaths throughout. The waters are gently alkaline and said to leave the skin smooth.
